lines.text: Last: how much can the motors still add at a given speed?
C T R E's dyno says a stalled Kraken X sixty makes nine point three six two newton meters, at four hundred seventy-six point one amps.
Spinning free, it reaches five thousand seven hundred eighty-five r p m. In between, torque falls in a straight line.
Why a line? Current is twelve volts minus the back E M F, divided by the motor's resistance, R.
Stalled, there's no back E M F, so R is twelve over four seventy-six point one: zero point zero two five two ohms.
Back E M F is motor speed over K v, fifty point four eight. At free speed it reaches twelve volts.
Torque, written tau, is K t times current, so it follows the same line, down to zero.
Our planning current caps it at one hundred fifty amps: a flat two point nine five newton meters.
Times gear ratio, over wheel radius, is wheel force. Times four, over sixty kilograms, is acceleration.
The flat part is twenty-six point three meters per second squared, up to about three point one meters per second.
Then it falls. Nineteen point oh at three point five. Nine point seven at four. Four point two at four point three. Zero at four point five three.
Draw the grip line at ten. Below about four meters per second, grip limits. Above, the motors do.
Braking skips this curve: back E M F helps there, so only grip limits braking.
